query: Benjamin Waterhouse Hawkins was commissioned to sculpt a series of life-size dinosaurs between 1852-54.  In this location, one species only had its head and back built with the rest of its body submerged underwater because they didn't know what it looked like then.  Where is this display located in 2024, which dinosaur species was this, and what did the rest of its body look like after all?
